entries.name: A Classification Theorem on Non-compact Embeddings between Besov Spaces
entries.abstract: We analyze the embedding properties between Besov spaces, defined on the total space $\mathbb R^n$ and on bounded domains. We give a complete classification on whether or not these embedding maps satisfy certain weaker forms of compactness characterized by the so-called strictly and finitely strictly singular conditions. The result extends the recent findings on Sobolev embeddings by offering a refined description of the quality of non-compactness in the setting of Besov spaces.

entries.name: A Bourgain-Gromov problem on non-compact Sobolev-Lorentz embeddings
entries.abstract: We study the non-compact Sobolev embeddings into the optimal scale of Lorentz spaces, $W_0^mL^{p,q}(Ω) \to L^{\frac{dp}{d - mp},r}(Ω)$, where $Ω\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $1 \leq m < d$, $0<q<r\le\infty$ with $1<p<\frac dm$ or $p=q=1$. We show that these embeddings are finitely strictly singular with certain upper bounds on the decay rate of the Bernstein numbers. We reduce the Sobolev embeddings to embeddings of Besov spaces and sequence spaces, which simplifies the previous methods by Bourgain-Gromov and Lang-Mihula.

entries.name: A polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of block-structured graphs
entries.abstract: The boxicity of a graph $G$ is the minimum dimension $d$ that admits a representation of $G$ as the intersection graph of a family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Boxicity has applications in ecology and operations research, where it models competition for shared resources. Computing boxicity is an NP-hard problem. Despite considerable theoretical interest, few graph classes are known for which the boxicity can be computed in polynomial time. Following the approach of Cozzens and Roberts (1983), we study directly the boxicity of graph complements, which we call co-boxicity. In this setting, the geometric intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ becomes a graph cover problem involving only complements of interval graphs. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that computes the co-boxicity of $G$ from two pieces of information about each block: its co-boxicity, and how the co-boxicity changes when certain subsets of its vertices become cut-vertices. Using this algorithm, we obtain polynomial-time algorithms for the co-boxicity of trees, graphs with bounded block order, block graphs, and cactus graphs. More generally, our method implies the union of these results: for any fixed $k \geq 3$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm to compute the co-boxicity of $G$ whenever every block of $G$ is complete, a cycle, or has at most $k$ vertices.

entries.name: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
entries.abstract: In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties. We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{χ_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.

entries.name: Stability of Anomalous Dissipation for the Forced Three-Dimensional Navier--Stokes Equations under Geometric Perturbations
entries.abstract: The energy dissipation in the inviscid limit is a central problem in turbulence theory. Kolmogorov's 1941 (K41) theory predicts nonvanishing energy dissipation as viscosity tends to zero, a phenomenon known as anomalous dissipation. Bruè and De Lellis constructed solutions exhibiting this phenomenon, but their construction relies on precise geometric conditions. Based on quasi-self-similar mixing, we prove that anomalous dissipation persists under small pure normal perturbations of the central curves satisfying area-preserving and equal-length conditions. The perturbations vanish near the spatial endpoints and at the initial and terminal times, and smallness is measured in a mixed norm with at most two time derivatives and total order at most six. We establish stability of the area-preserving maps and full local fields, including the mixed derivatives needed for Hölder estimates of the forcing, and obtain high-frequency energy concentration. A comparison estimate and a contradiction argument give a positive dissipation lower bound uniform over the admissible perturbations. Using the $(2+\frac12)$-dimensional framework, we construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional (3D) Navier--Stokes equations with anomalous dissipation for a sequence of viscosities tending to zero.

entries.name: A sharp inverse theorem for the quadratic large sieve
entries.abstract: We prove that if $A\subseteq[N]$, $|A|\gg\sqrt N$, and $|A_p|\le p/2+O(1)$ for every prime $p\ll\log N$, then $A$ contains at least $\exp(c\sqrt{\log N}/\log\log N)$ elements in the image of a single integral quadratic $m\pm x^2$. A matching construction shows that this is optimal even when the quadratic may be chosen arbitrarily in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

entries.name: Sampling Luck Masquerades as Allocation Gain: Auditing Test-Time Budget Allocation for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
entries.abstract: Neural combinatorial optimization (NCO) solvers report the best of many sampled solutions per instance, and the sample count is, by convention, identical for every instance. Whether a non-uniform allocation of a fixed total budget would buy anything has not been measured. We measure it, and we audit the measurement itself. First, on in-distribution workloads the allocation headroom is not detectable. Across three pretrained solvers (POMO, AM, SymNCO) on uniform TSP-100, an oracle allocation computed and evaluated on the same stored samples reports a 2.2-2.6% gain with intervals excluding zero; measured out of sample the same gain is indistinguishable from zero (0.457, 0.015, -0.512 percent). Following the customary in-sample procedure, all three solvers would have supported a published 2%-level gain that does not exist. We calibrate this bias against an instance-wise null in which the true gain is zero by construction; over the ranges we test it does not shrink with more samples or more instances. Second, the same correction that removes the phantom gains preserves a real one. Under distribution shift (a workload mixing uniform and clustered instances), a pre-registered confirmatory experiment finds that allocation guided by held-out sample statistics improves best-of-k by 11.5% (AM, primary endpoint; 95% CI [7.4, 19.7]) and 12.0% (SymNCO, replication) at equal evaluation budget, with the signal-acquisition cost not charged; a pre-registered negative control (POMO, an order of magnitude more robust to shift) shows -0.3% [-0.7, 0.24]. The gain exceeds a frozen distribution-label baseline by 4.2 points [1.9, 7.7]. An exploratory policy charging a 20-sample probe against the same budget retains 3.4% (AM) and 4.6% (SymNCO). We give a correction procedure and a reporting checklist, and release all data, code, and the pre-registration record.

entries.name: The Constant in Thomae-Type Formulas for Eight Points on the Complex Projective Line
entries.abstract: We consider the family of cyclic fourfold covers $C(x)$ of the complex projective line branched at eight points $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_8)$. It is known that the period map identifies the configuration space $X(2,8)$ of the branch points with a Zariski open subset of a quotient of the five-dimensional complex ball, and that the inverse of the period map is expressed projectively by $105$ automorphic forms $f_J$, which are proportional to the signed branch-point polynomials $\hat x_J$ with a common scalar factor. We normalize an element $ω$ of the one-dimensional eigenspace of the deck transformation group acting on the holomorphic differentials on $C(x)$. For the period $η$ of $ω$, we determine the common scalar factor: it is the product of a constant expressed in terms of the gamma function and the square of a quadratic form in $η$.

entries.name: The Operator Systems of Hankel Matrices and Complex Polynomials
entries.abstract: Using polynomial matrix spectral factorization, we establish a complete order duality between $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ Hankel matrices and complex polynomials of degree at most $2n$ on the real line. The projection construction and trace pairing identify $e_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}t^{2j}$ as the polynomial order unit corresponding to the restriction of the matrix trace. The Cayley transform relates these matrix orders to Toeplitz matrices and truncated trigonometric polynomials, but for $n\geq 2$ the polynomial systems with units $e_n$ and $(1+t^2)^n$ are not unital order isomorphic. We establish polynomial minimality and Hankel maximality, and characterize positivity of $C^*$-algebra-valued block Hankel matrices through completely positive maps on the polynomial operator system. An augmented Vandermonde decomposition describes polynomial states as trace-one positive Hankel matrices, with extreme states given by normalized evaluations and the leading-coefficient functional at infinity.

entries.name: The Dynamical Radius of Comparison for C*-Dynamical Systems
entries.abstract: We introduce a dynamical version $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ of the radius of comparison $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ of a unital C*-algebra, based on the dynamical Cuntz semigroup. We also give an intrinsic ordered semigroup definition, which agrees with $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ when $A$ is residually stably finite, and is lower semicontinuous for equivariant direct limits with injective unital maps. We construct actions $α$ of $G = \mathbb{Z} / 2 \mathbb{Z}$ on simple unital AH~algebras for which $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ lies strictly between $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ and $\operatorname{rc} (A) / \operatorname{card} (G)$, and actions $α$ of a finite group $G$ on unital C*-algebras for which $\operatorname{rc} (A, α)$ lies strictly between $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ and $\operatorname{rc} (C^* (G, A, α))$. For a minimal action of a countable discrete group $G$ on a zero dimensional compact metrizable space $X$, and with $α$ being the corresponding action on $C (X)$, we prove that $\operatorname{rc} (C (X), α) = 0$ if and only if the action on~$X$ has dynamical comparison as defined by Kerr. For finite group actions on simple unital stably finite C*-algebras, assuming the weak tracial Rokhlin property, we get $\operatorname{rc} (A, α) \leq \operatorname{rc} (A) / \operatorname{card} (G)$, and assuming weak tracial strict approximate innerness, we get $\operatorname{rc} (A, α) = \operatorname{rc} (A)$.

entries.name: The 3-adic Steinberg block and a categorical 3-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$
entries.abstract: We extend the work of Johansson-Newton-Wang-Erickson on a categorical $p$-adic Langlands correspondence over $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ to $p = 3$ by recontextualizing their construction in the Steinberg case. We produce a novel, more categorical method of analyzing the properties of this construction without requiring an explicit algebraic presentation. As input to this argument, we also perform some new analysis of the representation theory of the $3$-adic Steinberg block of $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$, obtaining results complementing those of Paškūnas.

entries.name: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
entries.abstract: We prove that the numerical range of a complex matrix has constant width \(d\) if and only if it is a closed disk of radius \(d/2\). The width in each direction is the gap between the extreme eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix. When that gap is constant, the midpoint of the projected interval is a rational function of the direction parameter. An operator norm bound and reversal of direction then show that the midpoints are projections of a single point, the disk's center.

entries.name: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large
entries.abstract: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. Moreover, $S$ can be chosen so that $|S\cap[x,x+1]|\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. This resolves the Erdős similarity problem in the large.

entries.name: The Symplectic Nature of Noncentral Reducible Stratum in SU(2) Character Variety
entries.abstract: Let \(Σ_g\) be a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\geq2\). The purpose of this paper is to use an explicit example, the representation of the surface group $π_1(Σ_g)$ into $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, to investigate the deformation space of the representation variety at a type of singular points, reducible but noncentral representations, and explore the geometric structure of the corresponding stratum in the representation variety and the character variety. In particular, the reduced tangent quadratic cone determines the symplectic structure at the reducible noncentral stratum of the character variety. Such a symplectic structure fits in the ambient character variety $χ\big(π_1(Σ_g),\mathrm{SU}(2)\big)$, where the top stratum of smooth points admits the Narasimhan-Atiyah-Bott-Goldman symplectic structure.

entries.name: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
entries.abstract: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective. This objective can control the error of the induced density when the growth rate is bounded. The algorithm divides the time interval into short windows. In each window, a frozen velocity generates the particle data for a regression of the network velocity. We draw the particles from period-adapted initial sampling distributions and weight them in the loss partly by their predicted future mass, because the reaction can make regions with little initial mass important later. We numerically investigate the method on the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) equation with a linear source term, Fisher-KPP equations, and Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao gradient flows.

entries.name: Repairing actuator schedules under graph constraints
entries.abstract: We consider a discrete-time linear system in which each actuator is assigned to one time slot. A graph $H$ records which pairs of actuators cannot share a slot. We seek to remove conflicts by exchanging actuators between slots, while preserving all tail reachability spaces. These spaces describe the terminal corrections available from each time slot onward. We give a sufficient condition based on the number of exchanges that preserve the required bases. The condition guarantees repair from every compatible starting schedule. Two bounds for checking it use failed basis tests and dependent column selections. Each accepted exchange reduces the conflict count, so the procedure uses at most as many exchanges as there are initial conflicts. An explicit family with unequal rank increments admits repair when $3N>4Δ(H)+4$, where $Δ(H)$ is the largest number of forbidden partners of any actuator. We also give a family of two-slot examples with only one forbidden partner per actuator and two initial conflicts. The basis constraints force every strict improvement to move arbitrarily many actuators, although one exchange suffices without those constraints. A second example has a connected conflict graph and one initial conflict.

entries.name: On complemented skew braces
entries.abstract: We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

entries.name: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges I
entries.abstract: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we fully characterize the asymptotic order of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ with $χ(H)\ge χ(R)$, where $R$ is any fixed edge-critical graph, and resolve the conjecture proposed by He et al. (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 159 (2023), 42-60).

entries.name: Exotic cluster structures on $Sp_{2n}$
entries.abstract: We modify the seeds of Berenstein, Fomin and Zelevinsky attached to reduced words for~$(w_0,w_0)$, for any simply connected simple complex algebraic group and any aperiodic Belavin--Drinfeld pair. In every type, moves of words act on the resulting seeds by mutations. After a change of coordinates introduced by Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the seeds are, for $SL_N$, seeds of the cluster structures of these authors, and for $Sp_{2n}$ they define regular complete cluster structures with the expected properties. This proves the aperiodic version of their conjecture for $Sp_{2n}$, with its uniqueness part in a refined form.

entries.name: Positivity in symmetric webs and block permanents
entries.abstract: We use symmetric webs to prove Marcus's block-permanent inequality for up to four blocks of every size, for five blocks of size at least three, and for any fixed number of blocks above an explicit logarithmic bound on the block size. The proof idea is easy: Bending strands in the Schur relation turns the comparison into a calculation with squared norms.

entries.name: Fixed-Point Results and Disequilibrium for Negators of Hyperbolic-Valued Probability Distributions
entries.abstract: Hyperbolic-valued probability distributions provide a probabilistic setting in which mass, order, and uncertainty take values in the positive cone of the hyperbolic algebra. We study the fixed-point structure of hyperbolic probability negators and the behavior of hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium along their iterates. Starting from a hyperbolic-valued metric on each mass stratum, we define the associated disequilibrium as the separation between a distribution and the uniform distribution determined by its hyperbolic mass. We consider the disequilibria induced by the hyperbolic Euclidean, \(\ell_1\), and Jensen--Shannon metrics. Their hyperbolic Schur-convexity is established and sharp lower and upper bounds are obtained. We also characterize the possible fixed-point sets of hyperbolic negators through an order-theoretic condition and derive criteria ensuring uniqueness of the associated uniform distribution. The behavior of disequilibrium along the iterates of hyperbolic negators is then analyzed through two complementary mechanisms. Domination by Yager's negator yields exact decay factors for the Euclidean and \(\ell_1\) disequilibria and a uniform decay factor for the Jensen--Shannon disequilibrium. Independently, Lipschitz conditions for generated negators lead to positive linear comparison maps whose spectral radii control the asymptotic decay of disequilibrium. These results provide structural and quantitative conditions ensuring that hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium converges to zero under repeated probability negation.

entries.name: A nonlinear multigrid method for the preconditioned lattice Boltzmann equation
entries.abstract: This work developed a preconditioned lattice Boltzmann equation (PLBE) smoother for the residual-driven full approximation scheme (FAS) multigrid to accelerate steady-state LBE calculations. To overcome the deterioration of LBE smoothing at low viscosity, we used a two- relaxation-time (TRT) collision model together with characteristic-velocity and kinetic precondition- ing to keep the relaxation frequency for the even-order moments within a favorable range, while independently selecting the relaxation frequency for the odd-order moments to reduce their local amplification factor. We further investigated F-, W-, and hybrid V/W-cycles to address residual stagnation observed with V-cycles at high Reynolds numbers. The 2D lid-driven cavity flow was used as a test case. At Re = 5000, TRT-PLBE-FAS achieves an approximately 27-fold speedup over single-grid TRT-PLBE. At Re = 20000 on a 20482 grid, the hybrid V/W-cycle reduces solution time by 14% compared with the W-cycle.

entries.name: Finite volume neural networks for singularly perturbed boundary value problems
entries.abstract: We develop a singular-layer enhanced Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) methodology for solving singularly perturbed boundary value problems. The proposed framework combines flux-conserving finite volume residuals with analytically derived boundary layer correctors, enabling stable and efficient approximation of sharp boundary variations induced by small perturbation parameters. Numerical experiments over a broad range of small perturbation parameters ($10^{-4}$ to $10^{-12}$), demonstrate that the sl-FVNN yields uniformly accurate predicted solutions and significantly improved convergence behavior compared to conventional FVNN methods. Further comparisons with sl-PINNs from (Gie, Hong, Jung, Appl. Anal. 2024) show that our sl-FVNNs attain comparable accuracy for reaction--diffusion and Burgers equations, while achieving significantly improved convergence for convection-dominated nonlinear problems. These results highlight the effectiveness of incorporating asymptotic layer structures into finite volume based neural networks, offering a practical and scalable framework for multiscale PDE learning in stiff regimes.

entries.name: Gradient estimates and monotonicity formulae for the $p$-filtration equation on Riemannian manifolds
entries.abstract: We derive Li--Yau type estimates on closed Riemannian manifolds and local Hamilton-type gradient estimates on complete manifolds for the $p$-filtration equation $u_t=Δ_pF(u)$. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and a structural condition on $F$, we establish a $\mathcal W$-entropy formula, entropy-power concavity and local entropy rigidity. We also prove a parabolic frequency monotonicity formula without curvature assumptions. The results include homogeneous doubly nonlinear diffusion and extend to nonhomogeneous power sums and the arctangent law.

entries.name: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
entries.abstract: We develop neural network methods for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations at a small viscosity $\varepsilon > 0$, whose accuracy is uniform in $\varepsilon$ and whose residual is evaluated on a grid that does not resolve the vorticity boundary layer. In the vorticity-stream function formulation with the slip boundary conditions, a vorticity layer of width $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ forms along the walls. The trial function of the singular layer Physics-Informed Neural Network (sl-PINN) contains the corrector of the asymptotic analysis, together with the law that fixes its amplitude at the wall. The amplitude is tied to the wall trace of the network itself, so that the method requires no a priori knowledge of the limit solution. The sl-PINN keeps the error uniform in $\varepsilon$ over six decades, for the Stokes and the Navier-Stokes equations alike, although in the latter the wall trace travels with the flow and is not known in advance. An enrichment that uses the thin scale but leaves the profile and the amplitude of the layer free deteriorates as $\varepsilon\to0$. Since the corrector carries the layer analytically, the Laplacian in the residual can be discretized by a finite volume flux difference on a coarse grid. The resulting singular layer Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) attains the same uniform accuracy as the sl-PINN, to within the scatter of the random seed, at about half the cost of a training step. The combination of the asymptotic corrector with the coarse-grid finite volume discretization is the main result of this article.

entries.name: Residual-driven lattice Boltzmann equation. Part I: framework and nonlinear solution methods
entries.abstract: We developed a residual-driven framework of the lattice Boltzmann equation (LBE) to integrate general nonlinear iterative methods. The nonlinear residual is constructed directly from the complete LBE collision-streaming update, allowing general nonlinear solvers to be integrated without modifying the original LBE algorithmic structure, i.e., the kernel consisting of collision-streaming, boundary conditions, and various forcing and interaction effects. Sophisticated techniques, such as weighted fixed-point iteration, full approximation scheme (FAS) multigrid, and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov methods are integrated into the LBE via this framework, and preconditioned LBE is further incorporated as a nonlinear smoother to demonstrate solver composability. Numerical tests validate that FAS and Newton methods do converge to the same discrete steady fixed-point obtained with the primitive LBE iteration. For the 2D lid-driven cavity flow, the FAS scheme reduces the measured solution time by a factor of approximately 44 at Re = 1000 and more than 224 at Re = 5000. Accurate results are also obtained for the steady flows past a cylinder at Re = 20 and the NACA0012 airfoil at Re = 1000. The low Mach-number tests for the flow past a NACA0012 airfoil further show that both the FAS scheme and preconditioning can not only substantially reduce the work required to reach steady solutions, but also mitigate the zero Mach-number crisis.

entries.name: Enumerating orbits of finite classical groups on their Lie algebras
entries.abstract: We enumerate the orbits of a finite classical group in the adjoint action on its Lie algebra, giving exact generating functions and very good upper bounds. We treat the general linear, unitary, symplectic and orthogonal groups, in both odd and even characteristic. In even characteristic, we get very nice formulas for the number of orbits on nilpotent classes both in the finite and algebraically closed case. We discuss the connection with commuting varieties.

entries.name: Toroidal Obstructions with No K_5 Minor
entries.abstract: Finding the complete set of forbidden minors for the torus remains an open problem. We determine the complete list of toroidal minor obstructions with no $K_5$ minor and prove that there are exactly $74$, each with between $10$ and $14$ vertices. Combined with the known classification of toroidal obstructions with no $K_{3,3}$ minor, this determines every toroidal obstruction that excludes one of the forbidden minors for planarity. The proof uses three-vertex cuts to show that, apart from $K_{3,7}$, every three-connected obstruction in this class has two distinct independent triples, each the common neighborhood of at least two degree-three vertices. The classification proceeds by considering the possible intersections of these triples and reduces each case by planarity tests and enumeration of the possible graph forms. From the $74$ minor obstructions we also obtain a complete list of $381$ topological obstructions for the torus with no $K_5$ minor.

entries.name: On the Morse index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations
entries.abstract: In this paper, we use the technique developed by the first named author in arXiv:2610.07815 to compute the Morse-index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations. For the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf fibration, we compute the index and nullity, where the metric on the $\mathbb{S}^7$ (resp. $\mathbb{S}^{15}$) is the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf--Berger metric. In particular, for the round metric on the domain, the Morse-index is $45$ (resp. $153$). We also give a spectral formula for the Aloff--Wallach projections. In particular, we obtain that the Konishi $\mathbb{R} P^3$-fibration $N_{1,1}\to\mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable throughout the two-parameter metric family, while the unit tangent sphere bundle $T^1(\mathbb{C} P^2)\to \mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable under some conditions on the metric. We also compute the index and nullity of the Clifford hypersurface in the fiber-squashing range of the quaternionic Berger family. Finally, for the identity map on the quaternionic Hopf--Berger spheres, we determine its Morse--index by an explicit sequence of transition parameters.

entries.name: COSI: A Framework for Robustly Valid Inference
entries.abstract: We introduce COSI (COnfidence from Scale Invariance), a framework for constructing confidence sets for statistical functionals. COSI builds on the HulC (Hull-based Confidence), which uses median unbiasedness to construct confidence sets from batch estimates. COSI uses scale-invariance properties shared by many common estimators. We divide the data into batches, compute an estimate in each batch, and retain each candidate parameter value for which the batch estimates pass a test of scale invariance. The resulting confidence sets are asymptotically valid under weaker assumptions than classical Wald and bootstrap procedures require, and their coverage can be closer to the nominal level in small samples. Applications include robust inference for the mean, regression coefficients in misspecified linear models, tensor norms, and Fréchet means.

entries.name: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
entries.abstract: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hytönen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(σ)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calderón--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(σ)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{γ_p}$, where $γ_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calderón--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-supremum terms. Together, the lower and upper bounds identify $γ_p$ as the optimal common logarithmic exponent and give the sharp worst-case growth $(1+\log A)^{γ_p}$ under the constraint $[w]_{A_p}\le A$. The results show why information from any one cube cannot fully capture the accumulation of a singular integral across many scales.

entries.name: Differentiable High-Order Mesh $r$-Adaptivity
entries.abstract: High-order mesh r-adaptivity typically entails minimizing a nonlinear functional using its gradients and, for Newton-based methods, its Hessian. These derivatives can be expensive to derive, must be updated with any changes to the functional, and errors in the derivatives directly impact the convergence of r-adaptivity. Additionally, derivatives of the r-adaptivity operator are required for consistent sensitivity analysis for inverse problems. This work develops a framework for differentiable r-adaptivity based on the Target-Matrix Optimization Paradigm. Given a pointwise functional defining the local mesh-adaptation objective, the proposed framework uses $\partial$FEM to automatically generate pointwise first- and second-order derivatives. These local derivatives are then assembled into a global gradient vector and a Hessian operator through the finite element operator decomposition. The derivative kernels support portable CPU and GPU execution, with partial assembly and tensor sum factorization enabling matrix-free application of the Hessian operator. The framework also provides consistent sensitivities of the r-adaptivity operator through automatically generated mixed derivatives and implicit differentiation of the mesh stationarity equations. Numerical experiments show GPU solve times comparable to those of hand-derived TMOP implementations on a benchmark problem, improvement in r-adaptivity convergence due to accurate computation of the derivatives, and demonstrate the use of mesh sensitivities for material-interface identification in an inverse heat-conduction problem.

entries.name: Directed triangles in oriented graphs without a directed cycle of length $3t$
entries.abstract: For integers $k,\ell\ge 3$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_k,\Cdir_\ell)$ denote the maximum number of directed cycles of length $k$ in an $n$-vertex oriented graph containing no directed cycles of length $\ell$. Grzesik, Jaworska, Kielak, Kuc and Ślusarczyk~\cite{GJ} systematically studied the generalized Turán problem for directed cycles and conjectured that, for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_3,\Cdir_{3t})=\frac{t-1}{4}n^2+o(n^2)$. They proved this asymptotic formula for $t=2$. In this paper, we prove it for every fixed integer $t\ge 3$, thereby confirming the conjecture.

entries.name: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
entries.abstract: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$.

entries.name: Real-Rootedness and Log-Concavity of Zigzag Eulerian Polynomials
entries.abstract: We prove that the zigzag Eulerian polynomials have only real, negative, simple zeros, and hence strictly log-concave coefficients, settling the first two parts of a conjecture of Petersen and Zhuang. Real-rootedness in combinatorics is usually proved inside a single algebraic framework, such as interlacing or stability. Our proof rests on a different premise: different parts of a zero set become visible in different representations of the same polynomial, and classical tools suffice once each part is viewed in the right one. The bridge between representations is a local rule. Forgetting the order in which a bounded-jump path visits positions leaves only a nearest-neighbor condition on sorted gaps, which makes an encoding via a transfer matrix much simpler to see. From there the argument passes to complex analysis. The sizes of the matrix's eigenmodes locate the zeros at the two ends of the negative axis, through Rouché's theorem. In a logarithmic coordinate the generating function becomes a combination of derivatives of the hyperbolic secant, akin to the classical derivative polynomials, and the arguments of its nearest poles produce a sine that fixes the signs between consecutive central zeros. The zeros are thus read off from the poles of an associated kernel. More broadly, the proof suggests that combinatorial polynomials defined by local constraints carry analytic structure, in their spectra and in the poles of their kernels, that is complementary to the usual algebraic methods and that classical complex analysis can exploit directly.

entries.name: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
entries.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

entries.name: Weak error estimates of a spectral Galerkin approximation to the stochastic Burgers equation driven by rough white noise
entries.abstract: In this paper, we investigate weak error estimates for a spectral Galerkin approximation to a stochastic Burgers equation driven by rough space-time white noise. The roughness of the driving noise results that the mild solution possesses only $L^\infty$-regularity rather than any positive-order differentiability order regularity. The theory of classical numerical analysis reveals that the convergence rate of numerical solution is determined by the smoothness of the exact solution, and hence $L^\infty$-regularity is insufficient to yield any positive convergence rate. Indeed, De Vecchi et al.\ \cite{DeVecchi2026} studied a spectral Galerkin approximation to such equation and only proved pathwise convergence. However, we aim to derive positive weak convergence rate for the spectral Galerkin approximation, which is determined by the roughness order of noise. To overcome the difficulty caused by the absence of smoothness of the exact solution, we turn to study the differentiability regularity of the first and second order Fréchet derivatives of the solution to a Kolmogorov equation associated with the spectral Galerkin approximation. We manage to prove that they possess nearly second order smoothness, enabling us to derive a positive weak convergence rate for the spectral Galerkin approximation. Finally, we conduct a numerical experiment to illustrate the theortical analysis.

entries.name: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem
entries.abstract: We place two disks inside the unit disk so that they touch each other and the unit circle. We then insert a disk of the largest possible radius, requiring it to touch both original disks. We show that the smallest possible sum of the three areas is $11π/18$, and find all equality cases. We give three solutions, using Descartes' circle theorem, inversion, and contact-point coordinates. The main difficulty is checking that the third disk is largest among all disks that fit, not only among disks touching the first two.

entries.name: Heat-wave semigroup estimates and the compressible Navier-Stokes Equations
entries.abstract: We study the connection between the heat-wave semigroup and the compressible Navier-Stokes (CNS) equations. On one hand, the parabolic-hyperbolic nature of the CNS motivated the study of space-time estimates for the heat-wave semigroup by using recent harmonic analysis development, in particular, the local smoothing estimates for the wave equations; on the other hand, we apply the new estimates to obtain global well-posedness for CNS in the optimal critical Besov spaces. For the latter purpose, we introduce a new iteration framework for CNS that exploits some intrinsic structures of the equations, so that we can successfully apply these estimates.

entries.name: $\mathrm{BMOA}$ and Carleson-homogeneous Denjoy domains
entries.abstract: Let $E$ be a proper closed subset of the extended real line that contains $[-\infty,-1]\cup[1,+\infty]$, and let $F$ be a universal covering of the Denjoy domain $Ω=\overline{\mathbb C}\setminus E$. We prove the conjecture of Huo and Zinsmeister that $E$ is Carleson-homogeneous if $\log F'\in\mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb D)$. The proof is based on an estimate for the length of $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ in terms of the Bloch seminorm of $\log F'$ and a weighted $L^2$ integral of $F''/F'$. From this estimate we deduce that $Ω$ has the Hayman-Wu property, and Carleson-homogeneity then follows from a theorem of Fernández. We also characterize these domains by Carleson measure conditions for the arclength on $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ and for the Schwarzian derivative of $F$, and by the $H^\infty$ interpolation property of the inverse images of suitable sequences in ${\mathbb R}\setminus E$.

entries.name: Finite sample guarantees of MPPI: suboptimality, sample complexity and closed-loop guarantees
entries.abstract: This paper considers model predictive path integral (MPPI) control for nonlinear finite-horizon optimal control problems with bounded inputs, allowing nonconvex and nonsmooth costs. We prove theoretical guarantees that quantify the suboptimality caused by positive temperature and finite sampling on MPPI and establish their implications for closed-loop guarantees. Specifically, we derive a suboptimality bound for infinite-sample MPPI that characterizes the effects of temperature and prior coverage, followed by a high-probability finite-sample approximation error bound that reveals the dependence on sample size, temperature, and cost variability. By incorporating these bounds into a terminal-constraint-free MPC framework, we further establish semi-global practical recurrence of the closed-loop system. Numerical examples involving a four-link planar manipulator illustrate the temperature-sampling tradeoff and the influence of prior quality on approximation accuracy and closed-loop performance.

entries.name: Continuous improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
entries.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

entries.name: The topology of the mean action spectrum
entries.abstract: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.

entries.name: B-Series Theory for Continuous Time Integration Methods
entries.abstract: B-Series are a common tool for constructing numerical integration methods and partitioned variations. In this paper, we expand the operations of B-Series to describe the formal expansion of modified differential equations found in multirate ODE solvers. Typically, such modified differential equations have time dependent approximations using summed fixed constant states. To create the B-Series we introduce a new operation called replacement to induce the constant states and add a time parameterization to the labels of the B-Series. By doing so we introduce new analysis via the permanent and block matrices which provide alternative formulations to composition and substitution. To support the time dependent labels properties are provided, the exact solution is described in Tree Iterated Integrals, and the underlying approximate representations are analyzed.

entries.name: Cyclic group actions on K3 surfaces and almost complex structures
entries.abstract: Fintushel, Stern and Sunukjian constructed exotic $\mathbb{Z}_n$-actions on $K3$ for $n=2,3,4$ using twist-rim surgery. We prove that these exotic actions do not preserve any Ricci flat metric or any integrable complex structure. This answers a question of Farb and Looijenga in the negative. In contrast, we prove that any smooth $\mathbb{Z}_n$-action on $K3$ for which the fixed point set has only non-isolated fixed points preserves an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class. In particular, this applies to the Fintushel-Stern-Sunukjian examples. Lastly, we classify the possible fixed point data and action on cohomology for cyclic group actions on $K3$ of prime order which preserve an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class.

entries.name: On the uniqueness of ground states for pseudo-relativistic boson stars
entries.abstract: We establish the uniqueness of both action and energy ground states for the pseudo-relativistic Hartree equation. The latter, for every prescribed mass below the critical stellar mass, proves the Lieb-Yau conjecture. Our approach establishes radial nondegeneracy and a strict monotonicity property of the mass-frequency relation, providing a unified framework for proving uniqueness in both variational settings.

entries.name: Extremal metrics for the $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalues
entries.abstract: We study the $G$-invariant Steklov spectrum of compact connected Riemannian manifolds with boundary, endowed with an effective isometric action of a compact Lie group $G$. Under a mild nontransitivity assumption on the boundary action, we establish that this spectrum consists of an infinite sequence of eigenvalues diverging to infinity. We then investigate extremal metrics for the normalised $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue functionals. Assuming that $\dim G \geq 1$, we prove that none of these functionals admits an extremal $G$-invariant metric. Moreover, when $\dim M \geq 3$, the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue is unbounded above even within a fixed $G$-invariant conformal class. The proof relies on a local model near a boundary orbit and spectral convergence under conformal collapse. Finally, in contrast with the upper bounds obtained by Colbois, Dryden and El Soufi for invariant Laplace eigenvalues of embedded spheres of revolution, we construct, for any $n \geq 3$, a sequence of smooth Euclidean domains of revolution in $\mathbb R^n$, all diffeomorphic to the ball, along which the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue blows up.

entries.name: Morse resolutions and applications to lcm powers
entries.abstract: We consider the $r$-th lcm power $I^{\{r\}}$ of a monomial ideal $I$, defined to be generated by the least common multiples of all $r$-element subsets of the set of minimal monomial generators of $I$. Some homological invariants of these ideals are studied. Specifically, we use discrete Morse theory to give sharp upper bounds for the projective dimension and total Betti numbers of these ideals. Moreover, we completely determine the extent to which lcm powers define the homological shift ideals of edge ideals. Finally, we study when the minimal resolution of some ordinary powers and lcm powers are supported on the same CW-complex.

entries.name: A Brownian web invariance principle: Localized disturbance flows and Hastings-Levitov(0)
entries.abstract: We establish a Brownian web invariance principle for localized disturbance flows, providing a criterion that strengthens the weak-flow convergence of [Norris--Turner 2015, Ann. Probab. 43, 935--970] to path-Hausdorff convergence of their full trajectory collections. We apply this approach to the radial, stationary, and cylindrical versions of the Hastings--Levitov$(0)$ aggregation model, proving path-Hausdorff convergence of the full harmonic measure path collections to the (Cylindrical) Brownian web, together with joint convergence of the full gap--finger collections to geometric embeddings of the corresponding double Brownian webs. This extends the radial HL$(0)$ small-particle limits of [Norris--Turner 2012, Commun. Math. Phys. 316, 809--841] for the harmonic measure flow and finite gap--finger collections. In the radial and cylindrical HL$(0)$, we also show that the rescaled one-arm domination time converges to a multiple of the global coalescence time of coalescing Brownian motion on $\mathbb T$, with convergence of expectations. The main new ingredient is a three-point survival estimate, proved via a multiscale stopping-time decomposition.

entries.name: Decision Stability and Model Reduction for Hamilton--Jacobi Navigation in Multiscale Flows
entries.abstract: Autonomous vehicles plan time-optimal routes through flow fields that are known only through reduced, finite-resolution models of an underlying multiscale flow. Classical Hamilton-Jacobi homogenization concerns convergence of the value function as the fine scale vanishes; but what a vehicle commits to is a route, and value accuracy need not imply route accuracy. We study this gap for a fixed-resolution reduction rather than in the homogenization limit. The committed route's dependence on the model-reduction error splits into two regimes. When the optimal route is a unique, nondegenerate minimizer with a regular value-function neighborhood, it depends Lipschitz-continuously on the reduction error, while the extra travel time from acting on the reduced model grows only quadratically with that error. When two routes are tied on the cut locus of the value function, the value remains stable, but an arbitrarily small change in the flow can switch the selected route, making route selection discontinuous in the reduction error. This dichotomy identifies where a reduced model must be accurate: not where the flow error is largest, but where the route choice is fragile. In the regular regime it yields a resolution-allocation principle, while an oracle marginal-regret benchmark illustrates the potential benefit of decision-aware resolution allocation relative to refinement based on flow-error magnitude.

entries.name: On Contractibility of Geometric Joins
entries.abstract: The geometric join of a family of sets in $\mathbb R^d$ is the union of the convex hulls of all colorful sets. For every $d \geq 4$, we construct $\lceil\frac{(d-1)^2}{2}\rceil$ sets in $\mathbb R^d$ whose geometric join is not contractible, disproving the conjecture of Bárány, Holmsen, and Karasev that the geometric join of at least $d+1$ sets is contractible.

entries.name: On Threshold Probabilities for the Stability of the Independence Number of a Random Subgraph
entries.abstract: For an arbitrary sequence of graphs $G_n$, we consider a random spanning subgraph $G_{n,p}$ in which each edge of the graph $G_n$ survives independently of the others with probability $p$. We obtain a general upper bound for the independence number $α(G_{n,p})$, from which, for an arbitrary probability $p=p(n)$, we derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, i.e., for the equality $α(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1))α(G_n)$ asymptotically almost surely, as well as upper bounds for the independence number of the random subgraph, including unconditional ones; for $p=1/2$ they recover A. M. Raigorodskii's results of 2017 and 2026. Under additional conditions on the structure of the independent sets of the graph $G_n$, we find, up to a constant factor, the threshold probabilities for both asymptotic and exact stability (the equality $α(G_{n,p})=α(G_n)$). Special cases include results on the graphs $G(n,r,<s)$ for growing $r$ and $s$, including Kneser graphs for growing $r$; we also give examples of complete multipartite graphs, graphs on the blocks of Steiner systems, and $q$-analogues of Kneser graphs.

entries.name: Grid-Responsive Pricing of Dynamic Wireless Charging with Coupled Residential Demand
entries.abstract: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) is an emerging technology that enables electric vehicles (EVs) to recharge while traveling. Its unique operational model creates two revenue streams for DWC operators through lane access tolls and electricity sales. However, these prices influence not only traffic flow and roadway energy delivery but also how much EV charging moves to homes instead, potentially within the same distribution network. Neglecting this coupling can underestimate grid loading and compromise pricing decisions. We develop a coupled traffic, EV energy, driver-response, and AC distribution network model with a model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes DWC tolls and charging prices while explicitly accounting for displaced residential charging and network losses. Using 78 days of I-210 West traffic data, we show that conventional MPC exceeds feeder loading limits on 52 days, whereas the proposed residential load aware controller eliminates these violations with only 0.6% lower operator revenue. Under a more constrained feeder configuration, it eliminates 50 overloaded days with a 0.9% revenue reduction. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of accurate residential demand estimation and feeder loss modeling, while peak-aware pricing further reduces daily peak loading by 3.7% relative to the base load. These results demonstrate the value of coordinated pricing that captures the interaction between roadway and residential charging.

entries.name: Training Neural Networks to be Locally Adaptive
entries.abstract: Deep neural networks fitted by global empirical risk minimization commit to a single model for the entire covariate space. In a regression problem, if the regression function $f_0$ is inhomogeneous --- varying rapidly in one region, while being nearly flat in another --- no single model can be appropriate everywhere, and the fit degrades where the function varies most rapidly. Here we study an alternative in which, instead of fitting the network globally, we fit it locally. For each query point $x$, a \emph{local neural network} is trained on the $k$ nearest-neighbours of $x$ alone, making the training sample and the fitted function query-dependent. We analyze the performance of the resulting estimator through a localization approach, establishing that the pointwise risk of the estimator with an appropriate choice of $k$ attains the rate $n^{-2α/(2α+d^{*})}$, up to logarithmic factors, when $f_0$ is locally $α$-Hölder with $α\in(0,1]$ and the covariates are supported on a $d^{*}$-dimensional manifold embedded in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. A matching Le Cam lower bound shows that this rate is pointwise minimax optimal. However, the local rate-optimality requires $k$ to be calibrated to the smoothness of $f_0$, which is unknown in practice. We therefore provide a locally adaptive choice of $k$ that makes the neural network adapt to the local Hölder exponent of $f_0$ and to the intrinsic dimension simultaneously, both of which are potentially varying over the covariate domain. An extensive simulation study demonstrates the dominance of the locally adaptive neural network over a globally trained network and several state-of-the-art methods.

entries.name: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks
entries.abstract: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. We establish that this model achieves flocking within finite time and derive a quantitative relationship between the lower bound of flocking time and graph volume. Based on these results, we observe that imposing sufficiently small flocking time induces an increase in network volume, and that larger initial velocity variance requires greater volume under the same time constraint. In our experiments, we trained a transformer-based PPO policy to select network structures at each time step. Under the most stringent time constraint, the maximum average number of connections increased sharply, confirming a threshold effect. The negative correlation between convergence time and average number of connections reflects the theoretical results well. This study provides quantitative evidence for the phenomenon that time constraints induce connection mobilization.

entries.name: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
entries.abstract: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line. The 19 displayed algebraic certificates comprise 18 improvements and one closed-form reproduction; they include HJ(4,3)>=164, HJ(5,4)>=7418, and HJ(5,6)>=34034. The underlying period-p construction also proves kappa_ow(t,r)>=p-1 for the one-weight bracket ceiling, in particular kappa_ow(5,4)>=7416 and kappa_ow(5,6)>=34032. Warm breakout-weighted tabu search on the type simplex gives HJ(3,4)>=51. Whole-colouring local search gives W(8,3)>522, W(11,3)>1193, and W(17,3)>3620. All accepted certificates are available separately and are checked by direct enumeration; unresolved searches are reported as UNKNOWN, not UNSAT.

entries.name: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
entries.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density-valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

entries.name: On continuous unitriangular matrices on \(\mathbb R^2\)
entries.abstract: Let \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) be the group of complex \(2\times 2\)-matrices with determinant \(1\). We prove that each continuous map \(A:\R^2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) can be written in the form \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1&f_1\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_2&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_3\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_4&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_5\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \] where \(f_1,\ldots,f_5:\R^2\to\C\) are continuous functions.

entries.name: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria
entries.abstract: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece. This relationship was anticipated by Bhatt and Mathew.

entries.name: An Explicit Parallelizable Robin-Robin Splitting Scheme for Navier-Stokes-Naghdi Shell Interaction
entries.abstract: We develop a novel explicit Robin-Robin splitting scheme for the system of an incompressible viscous fluid coupled to a time dependent Naghdi shell model. The shell model includes three displacement components and three independent rotation components, accounting for membrane, bending, and transverse-shear deformations. Both Robin conditions depend only on interface data from the previous time step, allowing the fluid and shell subproblems to be solved independently without coupling subiterations. For the fixed-domain Stokes-Naghdi problem, we derive a discrete energy identity that incorporates shell rotational inertia, interface velocities, and interface loads. We prove that the scheme is unconditionally stable for any fixed positive common Robin coefficient under homogeneous external data. Under suitable regularity and initialization assumptions, we establish first-order consistency and an $O(\sqrt{Δt})$ temporal error bound in the mechanical energy norm. Numerical experiments with a moving-domain pressure pulse compare the proposed scheme with the kinematically coupled $β$-scheme and a monolithic solver. To demonstrate its applicability to a more realistic vascular configuration, we simulate a stented artery using a bonded layered shell with stiff strut bands, capturing spatial variations in the arterial wall response.

entries.name: An Algebraic Approach to the Goldbach Conjecture
entries.abstract: We prove the Goldbach Conjecture using p-adic analysis and algebraic methods, requiring no knowledge of prime gaps or distribution. For $a \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{P}_a$ be the set of primes up to $a$. We prove that if a counter-example $2a$ exists, there is a monic polynomial $\mathcal{G}_-(z) \in \mathbb{Z}[z]$ where $\mathcal{G}_-(2a) = 0$. Applying Hensel's Lemma, we then show this polynomial structure forces each prime $p_i \in \mathcal{P}_a$ to satisfy $2a = p_i^{α_i} + p_i$ for a unique $α_i \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$. This produces a contradiction for $a > 4$ since each $2a - p_i > 1$ requires each $α_i > 0$ and the primorial, $a\#$, to satisfy $a\# \mid 2a$, which is impossible since $2a < a\#$ for all $a > 4$.

entries.name: On Iwasawa invariants of modular forms with reducible and non-$p$-distinguished residual Galois representations
entries.abstract: Let $f$ be the ordinary $p$-stabilization of the weight-one Eisenstein series, where $χ$ is odd and $χ(p)=1$. Under a Gorenstein hypothesis on the cuspidal Hecke algebra, we prove a factorization of the even branches of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function of $f$ by evaluating a cup product of cyclotomic units via local reciprocity. The odd branches follow from the Eisenstein specialization formula of Fukaya and Kato with a minor modification for the exceptional character considered here. We then obtain results on the $μ$- and $λ$-invariants. On the algebraic side, we compute the Selmer characteristic ideals at $f$ and the Iwasawa invariants of the higher-weight specializations. For every nontrivial twist of $f$, the ordinary characteristic ideal is generated by the corresponding $p$-adic $L$-function. On the untwisted branch it has one additional factor, the cyclotomic augmentation parameter. Imposing the strict local condition at $p$ removes this factor. For higher-weight specializations coming from newforms of level prime to $p$, Kato's divisibility then gives the cyclotomic main conjecture after inverting $p$.

entries.name: On completed homology and a conjecture of Venkatesh
entries.abstract: Let $F$ be a CM field and $Π$ a regular algebraic cuspidal cohomological representation of $\mathbf{G}=\operatorname{PGL}_2/F$. A conjecture of Venkatesh describes the structure of the contribution of $Π$ to the homology of the locally symmetric spaces associated to $\mathbf{G}$. We investigate this conjecture in the setting of $p$-adic homology with $p$ a totally split prime. Along the way, we elaborate on the relations between Venkatesh's conjecture and completed homology, the Taylor-Wiles method and the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence. Our main result is a `big $R=T$' theorem in characteristic 0, from which we deduce a variant of the $p$-adic realisation of Venkatesh's conjecture, conditional on various natural conjectures and technical assumptions.

entries.name: Equivalence Relations on Vertex Operator Algebras, II: Witt Equivalence and Orbifolds
entries.abstract: When can two strongly rational vertex operator algebras or 1+1d rational conformal field theories (RCFTs) be related by topological manipulations? For vertex operator algebras, the term "topological manipulations" refers to operations like passing to a conformal extension or restricting to a conformal subalgebra; for RCFTs, topological manipulations include operations like gauging (or orbifolding) a finite part of a generalized global symmetry or interpolating to a new theory via a topological line interface of finite quantum dimension. Inspired by results in the theory of even lattices and tensor categories, we say that two strongly rational vertex operator algebras are Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their modular tensor categories are Witt equivalent. Two RCFTs are said to be Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their associated 2+1d topological field theories can be separated by a topological surface. We argue that Witt equivalence is necessary for two theories to be related by topological manipulations. We conjecture that it is also sufficient, and give proofs in various special cases. We relate this circle of ideas to the problem of classifying RCFTs, and to lore concerning deformation classes of quantum field theories. We use the notion of Witt equivalence to argue, conditional on a mild technical hypothesis, that all of the finite symmetries of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model are invertible. We also sketch a "quantum Galois theory" for chiral CFTs, which generalizes prior mathematical literature by incorporating non-invertible symmetries; we illustrate this non-invertible Galois theory in the context of the monster CFT $V^\natural$, for which we produce two Fibonacci lines. Finally, we discuss $p$-neighborhood of vertex operator algebras, which is a special topological manipulation related to $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbifolding.

entries.name: Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for unramified maximal parahoric level
entries.abstract: We prove the Kudla--Rapoport conjecture for unramified unitary groups with maximal parahoric level structure. Our approach differs from the local proof of C. Li and W. Zhang. We reduce the conjecture to a global intersection problem using local-global compatibility. Then we apply an inductive procedure based on the modularity of generating series of global special divisors. This strategy follows the framework developed in the proof of the arithmetic fundamental lemma by W. Zhang and Mihatsch--Zhang and arithmetic transfer identities by Z. Zhang and Luo--Mihatsch--Zhang.

entries.name: On the Residue Sequence in Logarithmic Topological Cyclic Homology
entries.abstract: Algebraic K-theory participates in localization sequences, as first established by Quillen. We identify their boundary maps with the \emph{residue} map from logarithmic TC under the cyclotomic trace, resolving a conjecture of Rognes. As a consequence, we obtain e.g. a trace map from the K-theory of periodic complex K-theory to the logarithmic TC of connective complex K-theory. Moreover, we find that there exists a stable infinity-category C such that TC(C) realizes logarithmic TC for specific log structures, such as the natural ones on discrete valuation rings, connective complex K-theory, and truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. This provides evidence for the existence of a category of modules in the context of logarithmic geometry. We conjecture that such a category can be chosen to reflect additional structure on logarithmic TC, and we give evidence for this for discrete valuation rings.

entries.name: On a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture via categorical representations
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a complex reductive group. For a smooth affine spherical $G$-variety $X$ such that the stabilizer of a point in the $B$-orbit under the $B$-action be connected, assume that the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi-Sakellaridis-Venkatesh (BZSV) for $X$ holds. We establish a spectral description of a full subcategory of Iwahori equivariant coherent D-modules on $LX$ in terms of the relative Langlands dual of $X$, confirming a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture proposed by Devalapurkar.

entries.name: Functional Compression as Occam's Razor: Algebraic Complexity from Sensitivity Minimization
entries.abstract: Discovering discrete algebraic structures from data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning. We ask how continuous learning objectives can favor functional compression---representing data through shared algebraic composition rather than low-rank representations. We analyze the global optima of a canonical factorization model for algebraic completion (recovering finite binary operations) that demonstrated a preference for group operations. We measure algebraic complexity by the infimum of parameter sensitivity under exact reconstruction. We establish a universal complexity floor, whose attainment forces geometric alignment and unitarity of the latent representations. At the floor, input representations compose into the corresponding output representations; their reuse across the operation table propagates these local identities to enforce a globally shared algebraic structure. If the floor is not attained, a positive gap separates it from the feasible infimum. For cancellative operations, floor attainment forces the model's latent representation to be an injective homomorphism, equivalent to the target being isotopic to a group. In this case, every global minimizer is equivalent to the underlying group's unitary left-regular representation, up to isotopy and unitary gauge, resolving the central conjecture of Huh (2025). For non-cancellative operations, floor attainment forces exact structural redundancies (identical rows or columns) and is equivalent to a unitary factorization of the target's row- and column-reduced table with orthonormal output matrices, yielding the fewest distinct input matrices compatible with exact reconstruction. The resulting cancellative table then embeds in a group-isotope table. This analysis reveals a structural bias toward functional compression: at the sensitivity floor, algebraic composition of latent representations implements the target operation.

entries.name: On Pseudo-Effectivity and Volumes of Adjoint Classes in Kähler Families with Projective Central Fiber
entries.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the deformation behavior of pseudo-effective canonical divisors and volumes of adjoint classes in Kähler families. Based on recent developments in the Kähler minimal model program, for flat families with fiberwise canonical singularities, we establish the global stability of the pseudo-effectivity of canonical divisors and uniruledness, assuming in addition that one fiber is projective, while the same conclusion for Kähler threefolds is also true without the projectivity assumption of the central fiber. For a smooth Kähler family whose central fiber is projective with a big adjoint class, we show that its volume remains locally constant. Finally, using the (relative) minimal model program for Kähler threefolds, we verify the deformation invariance of volumes of adjoint classes and plurigenera for smooth Kähler families of threefolds, thereby partially confirming Siu's invariance of plurigenera conjecture in dimension three.

entries.name: Approximating parametric suprema for constructible and power-constructible functions
entries.abstract: We prove that one may approximate parametric suprema of constructible and power-constructible functions using functions within the same class. This resolves a conjecture by Adiceam and Cluckers, which was posited after studying a question posed by Sarnak. We apply our result to prove that a certain subclass of Cexp-class distributions is tempered and to make uniform a bound concerning pushforward measures.

entries.name: A counterexample to a basis conjecture of Brualdi, Friedland, and Pothen
entries.abstract: Brualdi, Friedland, and Pothen conjectured that certain rank inequalities characterize bases consisting of elementary vectors in the row space of a matrix whose nonzero entries are algebraically independent. We give a $4\times6$ counterexample: all the inequalities hold, but the four elementary vectors form a minimally dependent family. A construction using two planes in a common three-dimensional subspace explains the dependence and gives a second counterexample pattern with only four prescribed zeros. We also prove that the proposed criterion is valid over every field when the number of columns exceeds the row rank by at most one. A direct-sum extension gives counterexamples of size $m\times(m+2)$ for every $m\ge4$. Thus the minimum column excess permitting a counterexample is exactly two in every such rank.

entries.name: On perturbations that preserve the connectivity properties in tree percolations
entries.abstract: We consider a general bond percolation on an infinite locally finite tree, where the edge retention probabilities $p_e$ are replaced by $\min\{1,q_{|e|}p_e\}$, where $\{q_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of positive perturbation factors and $|e|$ denotes the distance between the edge $e$ and the root. If the original percolation model admits infinite clusters, it is of interest to investigate under which perturbations $0<q_n\le 1$ this connectivity property is preserved. Conversely, if the original percolation does not admit infinite clusters, we are led to study the stability of such a property under perturbations satisfying $q_n\ge 1$. In both cases, under minimal assumptions on the original model, we show that the percolative behaviour is stable against certain quantitative non-trivial perturbations. We also discuss an application of our results to the Erdős similarity conjecture for Cantor sets.

entries.name: Band edges of periodic Schrödinger operators are generically isolated and nondegenerate
entries.abstract: For periodic Schrödinger operators $H_V=-Δ+V$ with bounded real-valued potentials on $\mathbb R^d$ with $d\ge2$, we show that for generic potentials, each endpoint of every spectral gap is attained by a single Bloch band at only finitely many quasimomenta, and has a nondegenerate Hessian at every attaining point. This proves the Spectral Edge Conjecture for periodic Schrödinger operators.

entries.name: The Local Embedding Problem for Hardy Spaces of Dirichlet Series
entries.abstract: We solve the local embedding problem for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. For every $2<p<\infty$, the global $\mathscr{H}^p$-norm controls the $L^p$-norm of a Dirichlet polynomial on every unit interval of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1/2$: $\sup_{θ\in\mathbb{R}}\int_θ^{θ+1}\left|P\left(\frac12+\mathrm{i}t\right)\right|^p\mathrm{d}t\le C_p\left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathscr{H}^p}^{p}$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$, not on the interval or on the number and choice of primes occurring in $P$. The inequality was previously known at $p=2$ and, by taking powers, at every even exponent; it had been conjectured that these were the only positive cases above $2$. Together with the known counterexamples for $0<p<2$, our theorem shows that the embedding holds for finite $p$ exactly when $p\ge2$. The proof uses duality to control many critical-line evaluations together. A frequency decomposition isolates the contribution for which the relevant frequencies can nearly coincide. We estimate it by replacing the leading terms in the logarithms of the Euler factors with Gaussian variables, using the same variable for each prime at all evaluation points; the accumulated errors remain bounded. Comparison with a critical branching random walk and estimates for a finite-cyclic square function then give a bound independent of the number of prime variables. For $1\le p<\infty$, known equivalences also give the sharp range for the conformally invariant half-plane embedding, the reverse transfer of local Carleson-measure estimates, and boundedness of all characteristic-zero Gordon--Hedenmalm composition operators.

entries.name: Hull Games of Induced Path Convexities in Graphs
entries.abstract: In 1984, Frank Harary introduced the first convexity games in graphs, all of them based on the geodesic convexity, which is the graph convexity related to shortest paths. In 2024, Araújo et al. obtained the first PSPACE-hardness proofs on some of these geodesic games and generalized them to any graph convexity. In this paper, we investigate convexity games on several known induced path convexities: the monophonic $\mathrm{m}$-convexity and the $\ell_k$-convexities, based on induced paths and on induced paths of size at most $k$. We prove that the hull games $\mathrm{CHG}_{\mathrm{m}}$, $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ and their misère variants are PSPACE-complete for every $k\ge2$ even in graphs with diameter at most 3. We also use the Sprague-Grundy Theory to obtain a polynomial time algorithm to decide the winner of the games $\mathrm{CHG}_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ for any $k\ge2$ in disjoint unions of paths and cycles. For $k\ge3$ odd, we prove that Alice (1st player) wins $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ in the path $P_n$ if and only if $n$ is odd and she wins in the cycle $C_n$ if and only if $n=3$ or $n=α\cdot (k+1)-1$ with $α\ge2$. For $k\ge2$ even, the only periodic nimber sequences of $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ obtained through extensive computational testing occurred for $k=2^h-4$ with $h\ge3$, e.g, $k\in\{4,12,28,60,\ldots\}$. In this case ($k=2^h-4$ with $h\ge3$), we prove that the nimber sequences of $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_k}$ in $P_n$ and in $C_n$ are periodic and Alice loses (resp. wins) in $P_n$ (resp. $C_n$) with $n>k$ only when $n=3k+4$ (resp. $n\in\{2k+1,5k+3\}$). Finally, we show that, for $k=2$, the game $\mathrm{CHG}_{\ell_2}$ in paths $P_n$ is closely related to the classical game \emph{Couples-are-Forever} of J. H.
